The core innovation lies in replacing C51’s categorical projection, which minimizes the Cramér distance, with a quantile-based approach that approximates the return distribution using a mixture of Dirac deltas. This allows for stochastic gradient descent to approximate the Wasserstein contraction of the distributional Bellman operator. The quantile projection operator Π_{W1} maps distributions to fixed quantile midpoints, ensuring that the loss function ρ^κ_τ can be optimized via SGD. Theorem 1 establishes that minimizing Wasserstein distance via sample gradients is generally infeasible, motivating the use of quantile regression. Proposition 2 proves that the composition Π_{W1}T^π is a γ-contraction in the maximal Wasserstein metric, providing theoretical grounding for convergence. The QR-DQN loss function aggregates pairwise quantile errors, enabling end-to-end training without explicit support bounds. This reformulates reinforcement learning as a distributional optimization problem solvable via quantile regression.
